title: List 10 things people pay for in areas you like
builds: Picking one idea you can make a first sale with.
steps: Pick your finish time above, then set a 15-minute timer.
Write four headings: Music, Marketing, Money, Beauty and self-care.
Example: under Marketing, "make 5 Instagram posts a month for a local shop."
Under the headings, write things people already pay for that you could do. Aim for 10. They don't have to be good yet.
Star the 3 you'd actually enjoy doing for a month.
small: Write 3 ideas, one line each, and star your favourite.
check: You have 10 ideas, and at least one is something a person could pay you for within a month.

title: Work out profit, markup and margin
builds: Pricing your own idea so it actually makes money.
steps: Recall (1 min): without looking, write the 3 ideas you starred yesterday.
Worked example: it costs $2 to make and sells for $5. Profit = $3. Markup = profit ÷ cost = 3 ÷ 2 = 150%. Margin = profit ÷ price = 3 ÷ 5 = 60%.
Your turn: a custom playlist costs you $4 per client and you charge $25. Find profit, markup and margin.
Your turn: a budget template costs $0.50 per sale in fees and sells for $8. Same three numbers.
Guess the cost and price for one of your starred ideas and work out the same three numbers.
check: Playlist: profit $21, markup 525%, margin 84%. Template: profit $7.50, markup 1500%, margin 93.75%.

title: Learn the map of South America
builds: Reading any region by its countries, landforms and climate.
steps: Recall (1 min): what's the difference between markup and margin? One line each.
Play the South America countries quiz once. Write down your score and time.
Look at the landforms: the Andes run down the whole west side, the Amazon basin fills the north and middle, and the Atacama Desert runs along the coast of northern Chile.
Play the quiz again and beat your first score or time.
Write one sentence with your guess: why might one side of a mountain range be wet and the other dry? You'll check it next Wednesday.
small: Play the quiz once and write your score.
check: You can place Brazil, Argentina, Chile, Peru and Colombia without help. The Atacama is in Chile.

title: Cash flow vs. money that grows on its own
builds: Knowing what to do with the money your side business makes.
steps: Recall (1 min): name 3 countries on the west side of South America.
Read this: cash flow is money that comes in because you did work (a sale, a shift at the barn). Investing is putting money somewhere it can grow without your time.
Watch the compound interest video (about 2 min).
By hand: $100 grows 10% a year. Year 1 = $110. Work out years 2, 3, 4 and 5. Each year, add 10% of the new total.
Write one line: if your business made $200, how much would you keep for spending and how much would you invest? There's no wrong answer yet.
small: Write one sentence on how cash flow and investing are different.

title: Fix sentence fragments
builds: Writing an offer and messages that sound clear and professional.
steps: Recall (1 min): what does compound interest mean? One line.
A full sentence needs a who (subject) and a does what (verb), and it has to make sense alone. "Because I love music." is a fragment. "I made playlists because I love music." is a full sentence.
Read the Purdue page on fragments (5 min).
Fix these: 1) "Sold three playlists last week." 2) "When the shop opens." 3) "Ideas for a budget template."
Write 2 full sentences describing one of your starred business ideas.
check: Sample fixes: 1) I sold three playlists last week. 2) I'll go when the shop opens. 3) I have ideas for a budget template.

level: Level 1: Two sides of one event
title: The Spanish arrival in Peru: two points of view
builds: Seeing that history depends on who tells it.
steps: Recall (1 min): which mountain range runs down the west of South America?
Skim the Inca Empire page: how big it was, its roads, and how it ran without money.
Skim the Spanish conquest page: what happened in 1532 at Cajamarca.
Make two columns: an Inca family and a Spanish soldier. For each, write what they wanted, what they feared, and how they'd describe 1532.
Write one sentence: why might these two stories sound so different?
small: Write one line for each side: how would they each describe 1532?
check: Your two columns don't agree, and your last sentence explains why (different goals, losses, or who wrote it down).

title: Why one side of a mountain is dry
builds: Explaining climate with cause and effect.
steps: Find the guess you wrote on Oct 30 about wet and dry mountain sides.
Read the rain shadow page (5 min).
Draw it: ocean, wind, mountain. Show air rising, cooling, raining on one side, and dry air going down the other side.
Check your Oct 30 guess: right, partly right, or wrong? Write one line.
Tonight in a hot shower: watch the cold mirror. Write one line on how that's like a cloud forming.
check: Air rises up the mountain, cools, and drops its water as rain. It's dry by the time it comes down the far side. That's part of why the Atacama is so dry.

title: Score your 3 ideas with numbers
builds: Picking the one idea you'll test with real people.
steps: Recall (1 min): margin = profit ÷ ___?
Make a table with your 3 starred ideas as rows.
Columns: cost per sale, price, profit per sale, hours per sale, profit per hour, people you could ask, enjoyment (1 to 5).
Profit per hour = profit per sale ÷ hours. Example: $21 profit in 1.5 hours = $14 an hour.
Circle the winner. Write one line on why.
small: Do the table for just your top 2 ideas.
check: Every row has a profit per hour, and you've picked one idea.

title: Discounts and percent change
builds: Running sales and tracking whether you're growing.
steps: Recall (1 min): what's the profit per hour for your winning idea?
Worked example: a $25 playlist at 20% off. 20% of 25 = $5, so the price is $20.
Percent change = (new − old) ÷ old. Sales go from 4 to 6: (6 − 4) ÷ 4 = 50% up.
Your turn: 1) An $8 template at 25% off. 2) Barn pay goes from $60 to $75 a week. Percent change? 3) Followers go from 200 to 180. Percent change?
Watch the Khan video if any of these felt shaky.

title: Your first look-back
builds: Seeing your own progress and setting your next step.
steps: Look at your streak and how many tasks you finished on this page.
Write: the task you liked most, and the one that felt hardest.
Mixed recall: 1) markup on $3 cost, $6 price? 2) What is a rain shadow? 3) Fix: "Because I was tired."
Pick one thing you'll finish next week. Write it down.
Tap Copy my week below and send it to Mom or Dad.
Optional French bonus: write your winning business idea in one French sentence.
small: Tap Copy my week and send it.
check: 1) 100%. 2) The dry side of a mountain, where air has already dropped its rain. 3) e.g. "I went to bed early because I was tired."
